lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Opening echo of their mutual understanding, from the earliest days.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's ecstatic welcome gives their love a vivid, private image.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert's tender habit of shortening visits to take her hand.

lines.text: ‘Comfort me with apples, for I am sick of love!’
lines.note: The apple anecdote turns their travel decision into a shared private counsel.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Flush's sudden loss becomes a crisis they weather together.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Ba's playful claim that she is Robert's Flush and Flush is hers.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush's return, bedraggled but home, closes that shared adventure.

lines.text: For Flush, I did your commission, kissing the top of his head: then I took the kiss back again because it seemed too good for him just now.
lines.note: Ba carries out Robert's small commission to kiss Flush for him.

lines.text: What a glorious dream; through nearly two years—without a single interval of blankness,—much less, bitter waking!
lines.note: Robert's grateful memory of their long, unbroken dream together.

lines.text: I did hate so, to have to take off the ring!
lines.note: The painful removal of the wedding ring before their secret marriage.

lines.text: I can bring you no flowers but I pluck this bud and send it with all affectionate devotion.
lines.note: Robert sends a small bud as a token of devotion amid the hurry.

lines.text: And the dear, dear little bud!—I shall keep it to the end of my life, if you love me so long, ... or not, sir!
lines.note: Ba promises to keep Robert's bud for the rest of her life.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Her letters are so precious that even luggage weight cannot part her from them.
